The following words, terms, and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Alcoholic beverage means as defined pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-1-2(2) and includes all alcohol, distilled spirits, beer, malt beverages, wine, or fortified wine.
Dancehall or entertainment center where alcoholic beverages are consumed on the premises means any business licensed and open to the public on a regular basis as a dancehall, entertainment center, or social club which offers for its regular patrons alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises, and for which a license must be obtained for the consumption of alcoholic beverages on the premises.
Distilled spirits means as defined pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-1-2(8) and includes any alcoholic beverage obtained by distillation or containing more than 24 percent alcohol by volume.
Election day means one hour before the polls open to one hour after the polls close.
Fortified wine means any alcoholic beverage containing not more than 24 percent alcohol by volume made from fruits, berries or grapes either by natural fermentation or by natural fermentation with brandy added. The term "fortified wine" includes, but is not limited to, brandy.
Malt beverage means, as defined pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-1-2(13), alcoholic beverage obtained by the fermentation of any infusion or decoction of barley, malt, hops, or any other similar product, or any combination of such products in water, containing not more than 14 percent alcohol by volume and including ale, porter, brown, stout, lager beer, small beer, and strong beer. The term "malt beverage" does not include sake, known as Japanese rice wine.
Manufacturer means any maker, producer, or bottler of an alcoholic beverage. The term also means: (a) in the case of distilled spirits, any person engaged in distilling, rectifying, or blending any distilled spirits; provided, however, that a vintner that blends wine with distilled spirits to produce a fortified wine shall not be considered a manufacturer of distilled spirits; (b) in the case of malt beverages, any brewer; and (c) in the case of wine, any vintner.
Minor means an underage person under the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 3-3-23.
Open bar means any premises at which a retailer licensed pursuant to this article to sell alcoholic beverages derives 75 percent or more total annual gross revenue from the sale of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises.
Package means as defined pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 3-1-2(16) to include a bottle, can, keg, barrel, or other original consumer container.
Posts, chapters, and clubs of nationally chartered veterans and fraternal organizations means those organizations which, in the case of veteran organizations, are recognized as representatives of veterans by the Veterans Administration and, as to fraternal organizations, have charters from Elks, Moose, or similar organizations and which have complied with section 501(a) of the United States Internal Revenue Code (26 USC 501(a)) for a tax-exempt status.
Premises means the space or area owned, leased and/or controlled by the licensee and used by such licensee for the purpose of operating under the license, except that in the case of hotels and motels, the term "premises" shall include only the portion of the property where alcoholic beverages are sold. The term "premises" is further defined as one physically identifiable place of business consisting of one room or two or more contiguous rooms operating under the same trade name where alcoholic beverages are sold. Any premises outlet which cannot be determined as one identifiable place of business shall require additional licenses regardless of such establishment having the same trade name, ownership, or management.
Private club means an organization complying with section 501(a) of the United States Internal Revenue Code (26 USC 501(a)) for a tax-exempt status. The club must have been in existence at least one year prior to the filing of its application for a license to be issued pursuant to this article; it must have at least 75 regular dues-paying members; it must own, hire, or lease a building or space within a building for the reasonable use of its members, which building or space has suitable kitchen and dining room space and equipment as is staffed with a sufficient number of employees for cooking, preparing, and serving meals for its members and guests; and it must have no member, officer, agent, or employee directly or indirectly receiving, in the form of salary or other compensation, any profits from the sale of alcoholic beverages beyond a fixed salary.
Residence means the act or fact of living or regularly staying at or in some place for the discharge of a duty or the enjoyment of a benefit or the place where one actually lives, as distinguished from one's domicile or place of temporary sojourn.
Resident means a person whose primary residence is within the territorial limits of the city.
Restaurant means any public place kept, used, maintained, advertised, and held out to the public as a place where meals are served, and where meals are actually and regularly served, such place being provided with adequate and sanitary kitchen and dining room equipment, air conditioning, having employed therein a sufficient number and kind of employees to prepare, cook, and serve suitable food for its guests. At least one meal per day shall be served at least six days a week, with the exception of holidays, vacations, and periods of redecoration, and the serving of such meals shall be the principal business conducted, with the service of alcoholic beverages to be consumed on the premises as only incidental thereto. A restaurant shall provide at least 75 seats for customers.
Special events temporary license means a type of license issued to permit the provision of alcohol for any monetary exchange or transfer of funds and where the location of the event does not hold a retail, on-premises consumption license. This includes the selling of alcoholic beverages at an event (e.g., cash bar) as well as other methods for charging such as entry fees or donations. Licenses may be granted to for-profit or not-for-profit events under state regulations.

(b) No person shall have, own, or enjoy any ownership, interest in, share in the profits from, or otherwise participate in the business of any alcoholic beverage licensee in the city unless a full description of such interest shall have been furnished to the city council at the time such interest arose. It shall be the duty of the licensee to report to the council, within five days, any change in any interest in such licensee's business, including, but not limited to:
(1) Any division of the profits.
(2) Any division of net or gross sales for any purpose whatsoever.
(3) Any change in the payment of rents or leases.
(4) Any change in the ownership of any lease or building or land used in such business.
(5) Any change in the ownership of any corporation that has any interest in such business or the change of management of such corporation.
(c) After receipt of the notice referred to in subsection (a) of this section, the council shall notify such person within a reasonable time of any objection to the ownership or interest set forth therein, and it shall then be incumbent upon such person to dispose of such interest within 30 days after the mailing of the notice to do so by the council to such person at the person's address as shown on such notice of interest. If such interest is not disposed of within 30 days after the mailing of the notice by the council, or if no objections are filed within such 30-day period, or if such person fails to notify the council of the transfer or any such interest within 20 days after the acquisition thereof, then the license as provided for in this division may be revoked by the council until disposition of the interest has been made or notice given to the council of the transfer.
(d) The report required by this section shall be in the form required by the council. It shall be an amendment to the licensee's permanent license application, which is on file with the council and, as such, shall be under oath and verified as otherwise required of license applications.
(e) Whenever there is any application for an alcoholic beverage license, which application is the initial application following a suspension or revocation of a previously held alcoholic beverage license, the city shall call for a notice to be published describing the name of the applicant, the location of the business premises, and giving the time and date when the application will be considered. This notice must be published at least seven days prior to the application being considered. This notice does not pertain to the annual renewal of licenses previously granted by the city council. The license applicant shall be required to pay to the city the current sum as the cost of publication.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-73))
254:
(a) All applications for licenses to sell alcoholic beverages shall be made in person by the applicant, and in writing on forms furnished by the city, signed by the applicant in compliance with this division and shall contain, but not be restricted to, the following statements and information:
(1) The name, age, address, and length of residency of the applicant.
(2) The name, location, and description of the premises or place of business which is to be operated under such license.
(3) A statement of whether the applicant, or any person with an interest in the application, has made an application at any previous time for any distilled spirits, malt beverage, or wine license and the disposition of such application.
(4) Whether the applicant, or any person with an interest in the application, has ever been convicted of a crime other than for misdemeanor traffic violations.
(5) Whether a previous license issued to the applicant, or to any person with an interest in the application, has been revoked by any state or subdivision thereof or by the federal government and the reason therefor.
(6) Whether any other person is to be interested directly or indirectly in the profits or losses, or both, of the proposed business.
(b) All new applications for alcoholic beverage licenses shall be accompanied by a check or cashier's check, payable to the city, for the proper amount of the license fee. If the license is refused, such fee shall be returned to the applicant.
(c) All applications for the renewal of alcoholic beverage licenses shall be filed with the city prior to November 15. Payment of license fees for the renewal of licenses may be made at the time of application or by December 31 and, upon approval of renewal and payment, a license will be issued.
(d) The making of any untrue or misleading statement in the application for a license shall be sufficient cause for the refusal, suspension, revocation, or cancellation of such license, as the city council shall deem proper.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-74))
255:
Every applicant for a city alcoholic beverage license shall be at least 21 years of age.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-75))
256:
Upon receipt by the city of any application for an alcoholic beverage license or for the transfer of any license, the chief of police shall investigate and shall attach thereto the entire police record of every person named in such application.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-76))
257:
Every applicant for a license under this division, or for a transfer of such license, shall be fingerprinted by the police department before such license is issued pursuant to the authority of O.C.G.A. § 3-3-2.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-77))
258:
The city council may, in its discretion, require a personal statement of any employee of any licensed establishment for the licensing purposes of this division.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-78))
259:
(a) The applicant for a malt beverages package license shall pay to the city clerk/treasurer, at the time of application submission, the sum referred to in the city's schedule of applicable fees, as an annual license fee for operation for one year at one location or business where the products will be sold.
(b) At the time of application submission, the applicant for an on the premises malt beverages consumption license shall, in addition to all other fees, pay to the city clerk/treasurer the sum referred to in the city's schedule of applicable fees as an annual license fee for the sale of malt beverages, when such sales are by the drink. Malt beverages may be sold in posts, chapters and clubs of nationally chartered veterans and fraternal organizations for such annual fee.
(c) At the time of application submission, the applicant for a wine package license shall pay to the city clerk/treasurer, as an annual license fee, the sum referred to in the city's schedule of applicable fees, for operation for one year at one location or business where the products will be sold.
(d) At the time of application submission, the applicant for an on the premises wine consumption license shall, in addition to all other fees, pay to the city clerk/treasurer the sum referred to in the city's schedule of applicable fees, as an annual license fee for the sale of wine, when such sales are by the drink. Wine may be sold in posts, chapters and clubs of nationally chartered veterans and fraternal organizations for such fee.
(e) The applicant for a distilled spirits package license shall pay to the city clerk/treasurer, at the time of application submission, the sum referred to in the city's schedule of applicable fees, as an annual license fee for operation for one year at one location or business where the products are sold.
(f) At the time of application submission, the applicant for a distilled spirits consumption license shall, in addition to all other fees, pay to the city clerk/treasurer the sum referred to in the city's schedule of applicable fees, for an annual license fee for the sale of distilled spirits when such sales are by the drink. Distilled spirits may be sold in posts, chapters and clubs of nationally chartered veterans and fraternal organizations for a fee referred to in the city's schedule of applicable fees.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-79))
260:
An applicant for any license under this division who makes application at any time after January 1 and before July 1 shall pay the full annual license fee. An applicant for any license under this division who makes an application on or after July 1 shall pay half the annual license fee.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-80))
261:
(a) A licensee authorized to sell alcoholic beverages herein shall display inside the place of business the current prices.
(b) The exterior of each building where alcoholic beverages are sold shall contain sufficient lighting so that all sides of the building and entrances thereto are clearly visible at all times when the premises are opened for business.
(c) The licensee shall post in a prominent location on the premises, in a manner whereby it may be readily viewed by patrons, an approved sign setting forth or summarizing the laws of the city and the state in regard to the sale of alcoholic beverages to underage, intoxicated, or pregnant persons. Each sign shall be of a size and configuration approved by the state department of revenue and said sign may be made available to said licensee at a price to be established by the city.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-81))
262:
The city license issued pursuant to this division shall be valid only for the calendar year indicated thereon and shall expire at 12:00 midnight on December 31 of the year in which issued. A licensee that desires to continue in business during the next calendar year must make a renewal application, on such forms as prescribed by the city, for such year on or before November 15 of the preceding year. The payment of license fees for renewal of licenses may be made at the time of application or by December 31, and the license will be issued upon approval or renewal by the council and payment of the required fee.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-82))
263:
No license required by this division shall be issued for less than one calendar year, or remainder thereof, subject to the provisions of section 6-66, and, in case of the revocation or surrender of such license before the expiration of such calendar year, the holder thereof shall not be entitled to receive any refund.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-83))
264:
All licenses issued pursuant to this division shall be valid only so long as the premises is actively engaged in such business, with the exception of holidays, vacations, and periods of redecoration. If the licensee shall cease to be actively engaged in such business, the license shall be invalid and the licensee of such business shall immediately notify the city council and return such licensee's license thereto.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-84))
265:
(a) No city license issued under this division may be transferred from one person to another or from one location to another without permission and approval of the city council upon written application made.
(b) Any licensee desiring to discontinue business at one location and commence business at some other location must make a complete new application for such new business.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-85))
266:
(a) Where contrary to the public interest and welfare, no license to sell alcoholic beverages shall be issued by the city council for:
(1) Any person, as determined by the city council by reason of business experience, financial standing, trade associations, personal associations, record of arrest or reputation in any community in which such person has resided, who is not likely to maintain the operation for which such person is seeking a license in conformity with federal, state, or local laws, rules, and regulations.
(2) Any person who has been convicted under any federal, state, or local law of any felony involving moral turpitude.
(3) Any person convicted under any federal, state, or local law of a misdemeanor, particularly, but not limited to, those involving alcoholic beverages, gambling or tax law violations, if such conviction tends to indicate that the applicant will not maintain the operation for which such applicant is seeking a license in conformity with federal, state, or local laws, rules, and regulations.
(4) A location that, in the judgment and discretion of the city council, is not suitable because of traffic congestion, general character of the neighborhood, or by reason of the effect which such an establishment would have on the adjacent and surrounding properties, or on the neighborhood.
(5) A location within an area where, in the judgment of the city council, the number of alcoholic beverage licenses already granted makes it contrary to the public interest or welfare.
(6) A location at which the operation of the proposed business would be in violation of this Code or any state or federal law or regulation.
(7) A location at which a previous alcoholic beverage license has been revoked or suspended, and where, in the judgment of the city council, the problems which have arisen from operation of such a license at such location indicate that it is not in the interest of public health, safety, welfare, or morals that the sale of alcoholic beverages be permitted at such location.
(8) Which the granting of such license would constitute a violation of state law or regulations.
(b) No person, association, partnership, corporation, or other entity which operates a sexually oriented business as defined under this Code, or which is subject to or licensed under this Code, shall, after the effective date of the ordinance from which this article is derived, sell, distribute, serve or suffer the consumption or possession of any intoxicating liquor, beer or wine or controlled substance upon the premises of any sexually oriented business.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-86))
267:
The following shall be grounds for the suspension and/or revocation of an alcoholic beverage license:
(1) The violation by the license holder or such license holder's employee of any state or federal law or regulation, except misdemeanors or any ordinance of the city, other than misdemeanor traffic violations. The determination of whether any such violation has occurred shall be made by the city council and an actual conviction in a court for such offense shall not be necessary in order to suspend or revoke the license.
(2) The failure of the license holder or such license holder's employee to promptly report to the police department any violation of law or municipal ordinance, breach of the peace, disturbance or altercation resulting in violence occurring on the premises.
(3) Any conduct on the part of the license holder or such license holder's employee contrary to the public welfare, safety, health, or morals.
(4) Operating or conducting the business in a manner contrary to the public welfare, safety, health, or morals, or in such a manner as to constitute a nuisance.
(5) The violation of any state law or regulation or municipal ordinance pertaining to alcoholic beverages.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-87))
268:
Before the city council shall deny any application for a license required by this division, or for the transfer of any such license, or shall suspend or revoke any existing license, the applicant or licensee, as the case may be, shall be given written notice from the city to show cause before the city council at a place and time specified therein, which shall not be less than three days nor more than ten days of service of the notice, why such application for license or for transfer license should be denied, or why such license should not be suspended or revoked, and stating the grounds therefor. At the appointed time and place, the applicant or licensee shall have an opportunity to show cause, if any exists, why such application should not be denied or such license suspended or revoked. At the show cause hearing, the applicant shall be afforded an opportunity to present evidence, to cross examine witnesses, to retain counsel, and such other due process rights as may be afforded under applicable state or federal law. After the conclusion of the show cause hearing, the city council shall inform the applicant in writing of its decision on the application within ten days.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-88))
269:
No retail dealer who has a license for the package sale of distilled spirits shall sell or offer for sale or display or keep in stock at such retail dealer's place of business where distilled spirits are offered for sale any other product of commodity except the following:
(1) Wines, only if the retail dealer holds a valid and current license to sell wine at such place of business.
(2) Malt beverages or beer, only if the retail dealer holds a valid and current license to sell malt beverages or beer at such place of business.
(3) Tobacco products.
(4) Beverages containing no alcohol and commonly used to dilute distilled spirits.
(5) Ice sold in sealed containers only.
(6) Paper, polystyrene foam, or plastic cups.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-89))
270:
(a) A vendor may apply for a special event temporary license classification for the sale of alcoholic beverages at locations that would usually require a retail license. This temporary license shall authorize the alcohol licensee to sell alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises of the special event for a period of time not to exceed the hours of the special event or 24 hours, whichever is shorter. The vendor [may] operate for profit or not-for-profit.
(b) If the special event temporary license applicant has already obtained a city-issued retail license for on-premises consumption at a premises inside the city limits of Royston, the applicant shall complete and submit a special event temporary license application to the city clerk no less than 20 days prior to the special event. The city clerk may issue the temporary license if the existing license holder meets all criteria of the application. The applicant must obtain a license to serve alcohol at the special event from the State of Georgia and must supply the city with a copy of the state license no later than three business days prior to the special event.
(c) If the special event temporary license applicant is not already licensed for on-premises consumption by the city, then the applicant must complete a full application package required for on-premises consumption licenses and be approved by the city council for the special events temporary license. Applications should be filed 60 days prior to the special event. The applicant must obtain a license to serve alcohol at the special event from the State of Georgia and must supply the city with a copy of the state license no later than three business days prior to the special event.
(Ord. No. 1006, § 4(6-90), 3-23-2026)
271:
No license shall be issued except in a zoning district where the applying business is a permitted use as defined in the zoning code of the city.
(Ord. No. 1009, § 3, 10-6-2026)
Editor's note— Ord. No. 1009, § 3, adopted Oct. 6, 2026, added provisions intended for use as § 6-74. Inasmuch as there were already provisions so designated, said section has been codified herein as § 6-75 at the discretion of the editor.
274:
In addition to the annual license fees imposed and required in this article, there is levied and imposed upon each wholesale dealer selling malt beverages within the city an excise tax on malt beverages so sold, as follows:
(1) Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, such excise tax shall be computed at the rate of $0.004166 per ounce.
(2) All malt beverages, sold in or from a barrel or bulk container and being commonly known as tap or draft beer, shall not be subject to the excise tax provided for in subsection (1) of this section, but there is imposed upon each wholesale dealer selling such malt beverages within the city an excise tax of $6.00, for each barrel or bulk container having a capacity of 15½ gallons sold by such wholesale dealer within the city and at a like rate for fractional parts thereof.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-111))
275:
In addition to the annual license fees imposed and required in this article, there is levied an excise tax computed at the rate of $0.22 per wine liter, which shall be paid to the city on all wine sold, displayed, or stored in the city. Such tax shall be prorated on miniatures, half pints, pints, fifths, half gallons, and other quantities and on wine gallons so that each bottle shall be taxed on the basis of $0.22 per wine liter.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-112))
276:
There is levied and imposed an excise tax upon the sale of distilled spirits by the drink in the amount of three percent of the charge for the beverage to the public.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-113))
277:
There is levied and imposed an excise tax on all package sales of distilled spirits in the amount of $0.22 per liter.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-114))
278:
The tax levied by this division shall be paid to the city by each wholesale dealer on all beverages coming under this article sold within the city by each wholesale dealer selling, shipping, or in any way delivering malt beverages or wine to a retailer in the city, who shall collect the excise tax at the time of delivery, and shall remit the same together with a summary of all such deliveries on or before the tenth day of the month next succeeding the calendar month in which such sales were made.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-115))
279:
The summary report made by each wholesale dealer to the city shall show the exact quantities of taxed beverages, by size and type of container and the amount of excise tax collected.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-116))
280:
The city shall have the right to audit and to require the production of records from each wholesaler supplying retailers in the city and each retailer so supplied.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-117))
281:
(a) The failure to make a timely report and remittance shall render a wholesale dealer liable for a penalty equal to ten percent of the total amount during the first 30-day period following the date such report and remittance were due and a further penalty of five percent of the amount of such remittance for each successive 30-day period, or any portion thereof, during which such report and remittance are not filed. The filing of a false or fraudulent report shall render the wholesale dealer making such report liable for a penalty equal to 25 percent of the amount of the remittance which would be required under an accurate and truthful report.
(b) Such failure to make a timely report or remittance, or the filing of a false or fraudulent report, shall also constitute grounds for the revocation of the business license issued by the city to the wholesale dealer.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-118))
282:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell at retail or otherwise within the city any beverage taxed by this division on which the required tax has not been paid to the wholesaler or distributor or the city.
(Ord. of 2-20-2024(2), § I(6-119))
285:
The city council shall adopt through a resolution a map or maps with boundaries of the entertainment districts. All references herein to the "entertainment districts" shall refer to those areas that are specifically set forth. These boundaries may be changed by the adoption of a new map with new boundaries by resolution of the city council.
(Ord. No. 1006, § 5, 3-23-2026)
286:
Alcoholic beverage establishment means an establishment with a license duly issued by the City of Royston to sell alcohol for consumption on the premises pursuant to the alcoholic beverage ordinances of the city. For the purposes of this article an "alcoholic beverage establishment" also includes the licensed establishments further defined herein to-wit; brewpub, brewery or microbrewery, taproom and tasting room.
Brewery or microbrewery means a place where malt beverages are manufactured or brewed as authorized and licensed by regulation of the Georgia Department of Revenue prescribed by Georgia law.
Brewpub means any restaurant or eating establishment in which beer or malt beverages are manufactured or brewed as prescribed by the Code of Georgia.
Taproom means an establishment whose primary purpose is in the retail sale of malt beverages and wine.
Tasting room means an outlet for the promotion of a farm winery's wine which provides samples of wine to the public and for sale and as defined by the law of Georgia.
Specialty cup is hereby defined as a clear, plastic cup which shall not exceed 16 fluid ounces in size which is provided by the city to licensed alcoholic beverage establishments which shall contain a specialty imprint, decal, or sticker. The specialty cup will note the date of use written by the providing alcoholic beverage establishment. A fee for obtaining specialty cups from the city shall be established from time to time by the city council.
(Ord. No. 1006, § 5, 3-23-2026)
287:
It shall be unlawful for any person to sell, to serve, or to otherwise provide, with or without compensation, any alcoholic beverage in a street, alley, or parking lot commonly used by the public or in any other public place or on public property except as otherwise provided herein by an alcoholic beverage establishment licensed by the city. A violation of this section may be punishable by a fine amount set from time to time by the city council.
(Ord. No. 1006, § 5, 3-23-2026)
288:
(a) Those persons desiring to possess or consume off premises any alcoholic beverage purchased from an alcoholic beverage establishment as defined above which is located within the entertainment districts in accordance with the restrictions set forth herein are required to acquire and use as the container a specialty cup from the alcoholic beverage establishment within the entertainment districts from whom said person purchased the alcoholic beverage.
(b) Only alcoholic beverage establishments who are authorized to sell alcoholic beverages within the entertainment districts are authorized to issue specialty cups.
(c) A person's display of a specialty cup does not relieve alcoholic beverage establishments of their responsibility to determine if a person has attained the age of 21 years before dispensing alcohol to that person in a specialty cup or otherwise.
(d) Specialty cups are disposable and are intended for single use, to be determined by the date marked on the cup, which date is to be marked by the alcoholic beverage establishment.
(e) Specialty cups may only be issued by a participating alcoholic beverage establishment within the hours and days of sale as authorized by the City of Royston Code, section 6-22, "hours, days of operation."
(f) It shall be unlawful within the entertainment districts for any person to drink, attempt to drink, or possess any alcoholic beverage in an unsealed or open can, bottle, glass, or metal container, or in a plastic cup other than a specialty cup as defined herein, on the streets, sidewalks, rights-of-way, or parking lots, whether public or private. This section shall not prohibit the possession of containers of alcoholic beverages with unbroken seals.
(Ord. No. 1006, § 5, 3-23-2026)
289:
(a) Alcoholic beverages consumed pursuant to this article must be purchased within the entertainment districts from a licensed alcoholic beverage establishment.
(b) Subject to the restrictions set forth herein and within the boundaries of the entertainment districts, those persons who have attained the age of 21 years may be allowed to remove specialty cups containing alcoholic beverages from the alcoholic beverage establishment premises and may be allowed to possess and consume alcoholic beverages anywhere within the entertainment districts, including the premises of other alcoholic beverage establishment premises.
(c) No alcoholic beverage purchased pursuant to this article may be consumed outside the entertainment districts or upon any private property without the consent of the property owner. Consumption in violation of this section may be subject to charge under Code section 42-1, disorderly conduct.
(d) Each alcoholic beverage establishment within the entertainment districts shall have the discretion to choose whether to issue specialty cups in order to allow persons to leave its premises with a specialty cup containing an alcoholic beverage.
(e) Each alcoholic beverage establishment within the entertainment districts shall have the discretion to choose whether to allow persons to enter its premises with a specialty cup containing alcoholic beverages.
(f) Each alcoholic beverage establishment within the entertainment districts choosing to allow persons to either leave its premises with a specialty cup containing alcoholic beverages shall notify the city so that specialty cups can be provided by the city and so that the city will have knowledge as to which businesses are participating.
(g) Those businesses without an alcoholic beverage license may choose to not allow individuals onto their premises with a specialty cup containing alcoholic beverages.
(h) Persons are not allowed to possess a specialty cup containing an alcoholic beverage while in a motor vehicle.
(i) Any licensed establishment that allows patrons to leave the establishment with an alcoholic beverage in a specialty cup as provided in this section shall maintain posted inside all exit doors for clear public view a map of the current boundaries of the entertainment districts and a sign of at least 11-inches by 8½-inches that states the following:
"All Patrons leaving this establishment with an alcoholic beverage in an open container do hereby assume full responsibility to consume such alcoholic beverage only if it has been served in a clear, plastic cup not to exceed 16 ounces in size and obtained from an establishment licensed to sell alcoholic beverages within the Entertainment District outlined on the map below. Any individual who leaves the Entertainment District with an alcoholic beverage in an open container is in violation of the City of Royston Code of Ordinances and may be subject to a citation, arrest, incarceration, and fine pursuant to the Code of Ordinances." See Code section 42-1, disorderly conduct, paragraphs (20) and (21).
(Ord. No. 1006, § 5, 3-23-2026)
290:
The provisions of this article shall not be deemed to abrogate or otherwise impact any state law or local ordinance pertaining to public drunkenness, disorderly conduct, driving with an open container or under the influence of alcohol, or similar laws.
(Ord. No. 1006, § 5, 3-23-2026)
